data: Added with /fly mission JSON (#341 batch 5). Pioneer of asteroid sample-return + ion-propulsion for primary cruise. Successor Hayabusa 2 returned Ryugu sample 2020.
Yano et al. (2006) — Touchdown of the Hayabusa Spacecraft at Itokawa (Science)
First asteroid sample ever returned to Earth

JAXA's pioneering asteroid sample-return mission. Launched 2003-05-09 to Itokawa carrying four μ10 microwave-discharge ion thrusters. Survived a hydrazine leak, three of four reaction wheels failing, an ion engine failure, and seven weeks of lost communications before engineers nursed it back to Earth with one working engine assembled from the surviving halves of two damaged ones. Sample capsule recovered at Woomera AUS 2010-06-13 with 1500 μg of Itokawa material — the first asteroid sample ever returned to Earth.
First asteroid sample ever returned to Earth (~1,500 grains of Itokawa dust, sub-milligram total)
Japan's first Venus orbiter; recovered from a 2010 orbit-insertion failure to study cloud-top dynamics
ESA's first Mars orbiter; Europe's first planetary mission
First European Moon mission — solar-electric ion drive. Spiralled to the Moon over 13 months; deliberate impact 2006-09-03
First Mercury orbiter — 6 planetary gravity assists over 6.6 years to bleed energy before insertion in 2011
First spacecraft to orbit a comet (67P)
National Museum of Nature and Science
Hayabusa's return capsule, which brought samples of asteroid Itokawa to Earth (2010)
